Q: Select first approved or denied row if status doesn't change. Select last row if it does change from 'approved' or 'denied' A:

If I got it right - you want to fetch just the rows with the status IN('approved', 'denied') following the rules described in question. I presume your "first row" and "last row" refer to order by STATUS_DATE.
You could exclude the rows where status is not approved or denied and use the Case expression to check is there one or more distinct STATUS(es) left per SID and flag the first or the last (Min/Max) STATUS_DATE.
This will give you the filter condition (STATUS_DATE = FLAG_DATE) to get the rows you want.

SELECT SID, STATUS, STATUS_DATE
FROM  (   Select   t.*, 
                   Case When Count(Distinct STATUS) Over(Partition By SID) = 1
                        Then Min(STATUS_DATE) Over(Partition By SID)
                  Else Max(STATUS_DATE) Over(Partition By SID)
                  End as FLAG_DATE
         From     tbl t
         Where    STATUS IN('approved', 'denied')
     )
WHERE     STATUS_DATE = FLAG_DATE
ORDER BY  STATUS_DATE
SID STATUS STATUS_DATE
24 denied 2025-01-06 10:12:33
10 approved 2025-01-19 16:18:52
21 approved 2025-02-12 16:19:27
04 approved 2025-02-27 17:07:17

fiddle

NOTE:
If any of statuses change into approved or denied - the next execution of the code above will work the same regarding the first or last row fetching. That could be the changed row or not.

Q: Is there a sandbox, emulator or synthetic feed for testing a Datadog integration without real data? A:

I haven’t found any official Datadog sandbox with preloaded metrics or a LocalStack-style emulator.

What I did instead was mocking the Datadog API for unit tests (using recorded JSON responses) and for integration tests, I pushed synthetic metrics via the Metrics API (or DogStatsD) to a test org, tagging them with a unique run_id, and then query only those metrics. That way I could test end-to-end without running real infrastructure.

Q: ng serve too slow in Angular 21 A:

Looking at your prompt:

(David 2㉿DESKTOP-41LAC6M)-[E:\..\..\..\..\proyecto-angular]

You're running a zsh shell on Kali Linux over (probably) WSL2 but your project lives on the Windows filesystem (E:).

WSL2 has to cross the filesystem boundary on every file read/write, which is extremely expensive during compilation.

To fix the issue, move once the project inside the WSL2 filesystem:

┌──(David 2㉿DESKTOP-41LAC6M)-[E:\..\..\..\..\proyecto-angular]-[master] 
└─$ #--Making sure you are in your project dir at first! then...
  $ # Copy the project to your WSL home directory
  $ cp -r $(pwd) ~/proyecto-angular
  $ cd ~/proyecto-angular
  $ # reinstall node_modules in the Linux filesystem
  $ npm install

Now to be fair, that was clearly a git branch (master) so you would need also to map the new directory to git as well.

Anyway to run it now you'll need to:

cd ~/proyecto-angular
ng serve

Q: How do I update Google Antigravity IDE to the latest version inside the IDE itself? A:

How to Update Google Antigravity Without Data Loss

Currently, the "Check for Updates" button in Google Antigravity functions as a redirect to the official website rather than an automated in-app updater. If you are looking to update without losing your existing configurations, you must perform an "In-Place Upgrade."

Follow these steps to ensure a clean update:

  1. Obtain the Latest Binary: Navigate to the official Google Antigravity site and download the installer that matches your system architecture (e.g., x64 or ARM).

    • Note: Standard AI assistants may currently lack indexed documentation for this specific tool, so manual verification from the source is recommended.

  2. Execute the Installer: Run the downloaded file directly. You do not need to uninstall the previous version first. The installer is designed to detect existing configuration files and only overwrite the application binaries.

  3. Process Completion: The installer will request to close active browser tabs to swap the necessary files. Once the process completes, your previous settings, data, and configurations will remain intact.

Future Updates: This specific update introduces a native "Restart to Update" feature. Moving forward, the application will be able to apply updates internally without requiring a manual visit to the website.
